profiles.meeting_scenario: At a Helsinki-based B2B SaaS company, an Engineering Manager and a Staff Developer Experience Engineer meet to plan a six-week sustainability pilot inspired by recent Finnish industry findings on agile software development, with the goal of feeding practical input into the company's internal 'Software Engineering Roadmap 2030' workshop. The agenda is to choose which Scrum team and service will host the pilot, decide how sustainability will be incorporated into normal sprint practices, define what a 'library energy assessment' will involve, and assign owners for measurement, documentation, and workshop preparation. The expected outcome is a shared plan for the pilot's scope, timing, responsibilities, and what material will be ready for the August roadmap session.

members.name: Aino Lehtinen
members.expertise: Scrum delivery, backend platform coordination, release planning
members.background: Aino manages two product squads working on checkout and subscriptions at a Finnish SaaS company and is known for keeping experiments lightweight so they do not disrupt delivery commitments.
members.private_state: She wants to support the sustainability initiative without adding process overhead that could threaten a promised midsummer commerce release, and she hopes the pilot can be framed as a low-risk team experiment rather than a broader transformation effort.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' means a contained trial inside one squad that produces internal lessons, not a reusable company-wide rollout package.
The 'commerce/payments side' refers to the newer Checkout API squad she directly manages, because that is the active product area in her day-to-day planning.
A 'library review' means examining only direct application dependencies the team consciously selected in the service repository.
An acceptable 'energy baseline' can come from existing production observability data such as CPU, memory, and cloud usage under normal traffic, since the point is to avoid extra setup.

members.name: Oskari Niemi
members.role: Staff Developer Experience Engineer, Sustainability Initiative Lead
members.expertise: Internal tooling, performance measurement, developer enablement
members.background: Oskari recently started an internal sustainability program after interviewing Finnish software practitioners and has been asked to bring concrete practices to the company's roadmap workshop.
members.private_state: He needs the pilot to produce tangible artifacts that justify investment in sustainability tooling and training, and he worries that a purely local experiment will be dismissed as anecdotal.
hidden_assumptions: A 'pilot' should yield a first reusable playbook, checklist, and short training artifact that other squads can adopt after the trial.

The 'commerce/payments side' refers to the legacy Payments service and squad, because that system has better historical load-test data and is what people in platform discussions usually mean by payments.
A 'library review' includes not just direct dependencies but also transitive packages, base container images, and developer tooling that materially affect runtime or build energy use.
A meaningful 'energy baseline' requires a repeatable staged benchmark with fixed workload conditions, because production telemetry is too noisy for comparison.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'pilot' is supposed to produce
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to run a 'sustainability pilot' before the roadmap workshop.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the pilot is a lightweight experiment within one squad to gather a few practical lessons without changing how the wider organization works.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the pilot is the first version of a reusable sustainability package that can be shown at the roadmap workshop and then rolled out to other squads.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The word 'pilot' naturally implies both learning and limited risk, so each person hears confirmation of their own interpretation without feeling any need to unpack the expected deliverable in detail.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the team should do a 'library energy assessment' as part of the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a review of the direct libraries explicitly listed in the target service's dependency manifest, focusing on choices the team can change in normal backlog work.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a broader review that includes transitive dependencies, base images, and selected developer tooling because they all influence energy efficiency.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The seed topic already frames 'libraries used in software development' as a legitimate object of study, and neither person sees the need to spell out boundaries because the phrase sounds self-explanatory.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to establish a 'baseline' before trying any sustainability improvements.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the baseline will be pulled from existing production dashboards and cloud telemetry for the current service under ordinary customer traffic.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the baseline will come from a controlled staging benchmark using a fixed workload and energy-estimation tooling so alternative libraries can be compared cleanly.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They are aligned on the need for comparison and both regard the measurement method as an implementation detail, so the surface agreement on 'get a baseline' feels sufficient in the moment.

misalignment_points.topic: Which service is on the 'payments side'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about running the pilot on 'the payments side' or in 'commerce.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the newer Checkout API squad, which she commonly groups under the commerce area and can influence directly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the legacy Payments service, which platform engineers casually call 'payments' and which has richer benchmark history.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The company uses overlapping shorthand for adjacent services in the same domain, and because both systems belong to commerce, each participant hears the other as confirming the same target area.
